name: dish_pipeline_round2
frozen: 2026-11-16, before the analysis is run; no model or API call is made in this study
question: Among the links a model with web search provides for a dish, how many are public and embeddable, and how many of those are really recipe videos of the dish?
data: stored outputs of the second YouTube discovery study (candidates.json, judgements.json of data/youtube-discovery-v2/ in that clone), copied read-only into data/youtube-discovery-v2/ of this clone; not committed
links: model-provided links = the ids in candidates[dish].methods.B (method B: 'most popular, best-regarded recipe videos, up to 8, any language'); B2 is reported as a secondary source
pass_check: the server check of the target design: the video exists, is public and embeddable (candidates[dish].videos[id].usable); no title filter, no ranking, no count cutoff; the model's order is kept

relevance.agreement: share of identical labels and Cohen's kappa between the two on the same links
relevance.old_rule: J0: the normalised title (spaces removed) contains the normalised dish name from server/app/dishes/dishes.json

dishes: the dishes with both judgements and no error in judgements.json (27 of the 40)
metrics: links per dish: model-provided, usable (embeddable and public), usable and relevant (E and J1)
share of usable links that are relevant, pooled over links and as a mean over dishes
number of dishes with 0, 1, 2, 3 or more relevant usable links; dishes with at least one
share of dishes whose first usable link in the model's order is relevant
the same relevance shares under the old title rule J0, and the counts of links J0 accepts that E rejects and the reverse

failure types of the usable links E calls irrelevant, assigned by the assistant from title, channel, description and duration (judge reasons were not stored): neighbouring dish, other dish, vlog or eating show, short (60 s or less), compilation or advertisement, other
decision_use: Reported only. It tells whether a server without any relevance check (embeddable filter only) would mostly show real recipe videos of the dish; no pass/fail threshold is set because the design decision belongs to the owner.
limits: relevance comes from language models that agreed with one labeler's 60 labels at kappa 0.61 (barely above the pre-set 0.6) and judge metadata, not the video
27 dishes, one run of the model discovery, the dishes are mostly fried-rice dishes first in the list
failure types are one person's reading of titles and descriptions
